Features

# You Owe Me App Features

Track everyday IOUs in one running balance. Give important loans their own records. When a loan needs a schedule, add a repayment plan that stays aligned with real payments, reminders, and history.

New to the app? Start with the Quick Start guide to understand the core model before exploring every feature.

Want proof before installing? Read real App Store reviews and privacy details.

Best next step

## Find the feature for your situation

You Owe Me features are built around real money-between-people problems: unclear balances, Group Paybacks, awkward reminders, partial repayments, recurring costs, and shareable records.

## See the app in action

Explore the main YouOweMe features for tracking IOUs, Quick Split entries, Group Paybacks, shared bills, balance history, separate loans, repayment plans, reminders, PDF records, interest, and money conversations.

### Money between people

Start from people, balances, and the everyday money situations that happen between them.

### One running balance

Keep IOUs, shared bills, repayments, and partial paybacks in one clear history.

### Balance Sync

Privately connect one balance between exactly two You Owe Me users, so connected entries added or changed on either phone stay aligned.

### Relationship Timeline

See repayments, statements, follow-ups, Group Paybacks, and Loan Records in one chronological history with each person.

### Separate loans

Keep each loan named and separate, with its own balance and history, while everything still counts toward the full balance with that person.

### Repayment plans

Compare practical payoff options, then keep the schedule current as real payments are recorded.

### Know when to follow up

Smart Money Check-Ins help you notice when silence, promised dates, or repayment progress need attention.

### Know what to say

Money Conversations turn the real balance and history into calmer follow-up, ask-for-loan, and repayment update messages.

### Share a live balance

Share an always-current balance in a browser link without requiring the other person to install the app.

### Split Entry

Create one shared expense, split it equally or exactly, and save clean per-person balances without duplicate entries.

### Group Paybacks

Track a shared cost you paid for until everyone pays. See who paid, who partially paid, and who still owes while each person’s balance stays correct.

### Recurring bills

Use recurring entries for rent, utilities, subscriptions, allowances, and repeated household or family costs.

### Payment reminders

Set reminders for due dates, bills, balances, and follow-ups, then come back to the right person or payment when it needs attention.

### Share clear records

Create clear PDF statements for family reimbursements, clients, larger balances, or formal summaries.

### Track interest

Add percentage interest that grows over time, or add one fixed interest amount when the extra charge is already agreed.

### Log money by voice

Capture real-world money moments quickly by speaking naturally instead of typing every detail.

## Balance & records

Keep the actual money story clear: who paid, who repaid, what changed, what was shared, and where things stand now.

### Running balances

Every entry updates one clear balance per person, so you can see who owes whom without rebuilding the history from chats, notes, bank transfers, or memory.

This is also useful for temporary support, where one person covers rent, groceries, bills, or other help and repayments happen later in steps.

With Balance Replay, you can scroll back through entries and see who owed what around the moment you are reviewing.

Learn what a running balance means and how it works.

If you are still deciding whether notes, spreadsheets, payment history, calculators, split apps, or You Owe Me fit best, compare the best way to track IOUs between people.

- Long-running IOUs with friends or family

- Couple, roommate, or client balances that change over time

- Partial repayments and shared expenses in one balance history

See how this applies to roommate bills and shared household costs.

### Balance Replay

Scroll through your entry history and the balance updates with the moment you are viewing. Instead of seeing only today's total, you can understand who owed what around older entries, repayments, and interest as it stood then. Percentage interest is date-aware; fixed interest stays as the one amount added to the entry.

- Checking what was owed before or after a repayment

- Seeing who owed what around an older entry

- Noticing when a balance changed direction

- Reviewing percentage interest using the date being shown

### Loan Records

Loan Records keep each loan in its own record without creating another person or losing the wider history between you.

Name a car repair, rent deposit, laptop purchase, family loan, or other balance that deserves its own view. Each loan keeps its own remaining balance, updates, interest terms, status, and optional repayment plan.

The same person can have several loans at once without mixing their purposes together. Every linked payment or update still contributes to that person’s overall balance.

You can also start with an already-in-progress loan: enter what remains today, keep the real historical start date, and add paid-before-tracking context without inventing old transactions.

For support that should be repaid gradually, Loan Records can keep one temporary support arrangement separate while the full person balance stays correct.

For the real-life helper-side situation, read how to support someone financially without confusion before turning support into a clear record.

If you only need a quick written note before opening a Loan Record, use the Temporary Financial Support Record Template to capture what was covered, what should happen next, and the check-in date.

If you only need a one-time no-interest calculation, use the free Payment Plan Calculator. When the schedule needs to stay tied to the loan balance and payments, add a repayment plan in the app.

Each loan stays visible in Timeline too, including when it started, when its plan changed, and when it was settled.

- Larger or longer-running loans

- Multiple balances with the same person

- Repayments that need to stay tied to the right loan

- Family loans, rent deposits, larger purchases, repairs, or existing loans brought into the app

### Repayment plans that stay current

Add an optional plan to any active loan when “pay it back later” needs a clearer path. Choose weekly, every-two-weeks, or monthly payments and set the first payment date.

Start from the decision that is easiest to make: compare lower-payment, balanced, and faster-payoff options; enter a regular payment amount; choose a projected payoff date; or choose the number of payments. The app calculates the rest before you save.

The plan uses the same balance and payment history as the loan. If a payment is smaller than planned, the app shows what is still needed for that installment. If it is larger, the extra amount can move the plan ahead. Additional borrowing, corrections, or deleted entries update the remaining schedule, projected payoff, and next reminder.

See what is due next and whether the plan is on track, ahead, due today, or overdue. Interest can be left out, added as one agreed fixed amount, or calculated on the declining unpaid balance.

If circumstances change, start a revised plan from the current balance while keeping the earlier plan in history. Ending a plan stops future schedule tracking and its reminder without deleting the loan or its payments. One active repayment plan is included for free; paid access supports unlimited active plans.

See how a named personal loan stays current after partial, extra, early, or late payments.

Need the manual method first? See what to record for one personal loan before creating a Loan Record.

- Personal or family loans repaid over time

- Plans built around an affordable payment or target date

- Partial, extra, early, or late payments

- Loans that were already underway before tracking began

- Changing a plan without erasing the earlier plan history

- Keeping the next amount, date, and projected payoff current

### Relationship Timeline

Timeline connects money movement with money communication. For each person, it brings balance changes, repayments, separate loans, repayment-plan starts and changes, plan-linked payments, follow-ups, repayment updates, loan requests, and shared records into one chronological view.

It can also surface the loan and amount that need attention next—overdue first, then due today, then upcoming—and stays quiet when no action is needed.

- Seeing the full history with one person

- Checking when you last followed up or sent an update

- Keeping separate loans, plan milestones, and plan-linked payments visible inside the relationship

- Seeing when you shared a statement, PDF, Live Link, text history, or CSV export

- Understanding balance phases, settlements, and direction changes

- Seeing a clearer next step before another money conversation

### Group Paybacks

Group Paybacks organize one shared thing you paid for — a gift, tickets, dinner, deposit, booking, or small shared purchase — while each person’s real share stays in their own balance history.

Use it when the question is not only “what was the split?” but “who has paid me back, who partly paid, and who still owes?”

- Group gifts

- Tickets and bookings

- Dinner or shared purchase paid by you

- Deposits or reservations

- Office/team gifts

- Small roommate or family shared costs

Group Paybacks are not full trip accounting or a collaborative group ledger. They are best when you paid first and want to track paybacks from each person.

Need a quick status check first? Use the Group Payback Calculator. Need the simple tracking workflow first? Read how to track who paid you back for a group expense.

### IOU tracking

Record money lent, money borrowed, informal loans, covered purchases, and everyday IOUs without turning the app into accounting software.

- Money a friend still owes you

- Money you borrowed and want to repay clearly

- Family loans, client balances, and personal payback records

### Borrow/lend history

Keep the everyday entry history clear, whether you lent money, borrowed money, paid for something, or received a repayment. The point is to preserve context before details fade.

- Checking how a balance got to its current amount

- Confirming old repayments or partial payments

- Keeping a record for family or client conversations

### Partial repayments

Record a repayment even when it does not settle the full amount. The running balance updates immediately, which keeps follow-ups fair and specific. On an active repayment plan, the app shows what the current installment still needs and updates the next reminder to that amount. Need the message wording too? Read how to follow up after someone pays only part.

- Someone pays back part of an IOU

- You repay a balance in stages

- Client or family balances move gradually over time

### Notes and entry history

Add context to entries so the future version of you knows what the payment was for. Notes help turn a number into a story both sides can understand.

- Groceries, rent, subscriptions, online orders, and travel

- Explaining a repayment or adjustment

- Keeping cleaner records for formal statements

### Search and quick entry

Find older amounts or notes quickly and add new entries without friction, especially when you track money often.

- Large histories with many entries

- Frequent family reimbursements or household purchases

- Fast capture before details are forgotten

### Multi-currency support

Track balances in different currencies when the real-life situation crosses countries, travel, or people who pay in different currencies.

- Travel expenses and international friends

- Family purchases in different currencies

- Separate balances that should not be merged into one currency

### CSV export

Export records when you need a spreadsheet backup, want to review your history elsewhere, or need to preserve data outside the app. Timeline can also show when a CSV history was exported, so sharing and export actions do not disappear from context.

Trying to decide whether a spreadsheet is enough? Start with the broader best way to track IOUs between people comparison, then read the spreadsheet vs app comparison for tracking money owed.

- Personal backups

- Tax-time or client record review

- Moving records into a spreadsheet for analysis

## Communication & sharing

The app does not only store numbers. It helps you decide when communication matters, what to say next, and what context you already shared.

### Smart Money Check-Ins

Silence is often what makes money situations awkward. Smart Money Check-Ins adds a proactive timing layer by watching real balances, repayment progress, reminders, promised dates, and stretches of silence.

When communication starts to matter, the app suggests the right next step, explains why now, and takes you into a ready-to-send message before tension has time to grow. Timeline places that guidance next to the relationship history that explains it. If you already know you need more time, read how to send a repayment update when you need more time.

- Following up when someone owes you and silence is becoming risky

- Sending a repayment update when you owe someone

- Avoiding repetitive prompts with adaptive resurfacing

### Money Conversations

Money Conversations turns your real balance and history into ready-to-send messages for the three situations people avoid most: Follow-Up, Ask for Loan, and Repayment Update.

For temporary support, this helps turn the real balance into a calm ask, repayment update, or request for more time. For a manual starting point, use the repayment update guide.

Choose a tone, adjust details if needed, and keep full control before sending. Messages can include a Live Link so the other person can view the latest statement without installing the app. When you copy or share a Money Conversation, Timeline can record that the communication happened.

Money Conversations can help with clear money messages after you choose to ask, lend, follow up, or update someone. If the right answer is not to lend at all, read how to politely say no when people ask for money.

Need a one-time manual message first? Read the polite reminder guide or browse repayment reminder examples.

- Follow-up when someone owes you

- Ask for Loan when you need help and want to ask respectfully

- Repayment Update when you owe someone and want to keep trust intact

### Follow-Up messages

Generate a clear check-in when someone still owes you and you want the message to feel calm, specific, and grounded in the actual balance. Timeline helps you see whether you already followed up recently or shared the details another way.

- Late repayments

- Friendly reminders after silence

- Awkward IOUs where wording matters

### Ask for Loan messages

When you need to borrow money, create a clearer request from the real context instead of rewriting the message until it feels acceptable.

For a manual starting point before using Money Conversations, read how to ask family for temporary financial help clearly.

- Asking a friend or family member for help

- Explaining amount, reason, and expectations

- Keeping the tone respectful and direct

### Repayment Update messages

If you owe someone, send a clear update that explains what changed, what has been repaid, and where things stand now. Timeline can show when you sent a repayment update, which makes the next message easier to judge. If you need more time before the next payment, use the repayment update guide. If you are sending a partial repayment yourself, the same guide includes a responsible partial repayment update example.

- Confirming a partial repayment

- Keeping trust when you need more time

- Reducing confusion about the remaining balance

Balance Sync

### Keep one balance updated in both apps

Connect a balance with someone you trust. Add or update an entry on either phone, and Balance Sync keeps both apps up to date—without sending changes back and forth.

Both people see the same underlying activity and an up-to-date balance from their own perspective. Each person keeps a separate record in their app, so Balance Sync adds two-way participation without turning the balance into a group workspace.

- Private, two-way connection for exactly two You Owe Me users

- Add, edit, archive, or delete supported connected entries from either phone

- Offline changes stay safely stored and synchronize after connectivity returns

- Clear sync status and explicit conflict handling—no silent overwrites

- Names, profile images, reminders, recurrence rules, and attachments stay local

You do not need the same setup for every balance. Choose based on whether the other person only needs visibility or also needs to update the record.

### Share an always-current balance without requiring the app

You keep the record in You Owe Me. The other person opens one read-only browser link to see the latest balance and history as you update it—without installing the app or creating an account.

Use Live Link when the other person needs visibility but does not need to edit the balance. The same link remains useful as entries, repayments, and the current balance change.

If the main question is whether everyone needs to install the same app, read the one-person shared-money tracking guide.

- Sharing a live balance with family, partners, roommates, or clients

- Replacing repeated screenshots with one current link

- Giving the other person visibility without asking them to install the app

### Shareable summaries

Send clear summaries when the other person needs context, whether that is a quick balance explanation, a Live Link, or a more formal PDF statement. Timeline records sharing and export events, so those moments stay part of the money story.

- Reducing back-and-forth questions

- Sharing a balance before a conversation

- Giving people a record they can review later

### Comparing YouOweMe with group expense apps?

If you are choosing between collaborative group splitting and You Owe Me’s private running-balance model — including Group Paybacks for shared costs you paid for — compare YouOweMe with Splitwise. If the decision is broader than one brand and you are choosing between a shared expense app and a running balance app, use the focused comparison.

- Deciding whether everyone needs to join the same expense ledger

- Choosing between a quick split, a Group Payback, and one clear per-person balance

- Understanding when Live Links and Money Conversations matter more than a group record

## Balance Sync FAQ

### Do both people need You Owe Me for Balance Sync?

Yes. Balance Sync connects exactly two You Owe Me users. Both participants need full Sign in with Apple accounts and a compatible version of the app, currently You Owe Me 6.9.4 or later. If only one person wants the app, use Live Link or another shareable summary instead.

### How is Balance Sync different from Live Link?

Live Link is the one-way option: one person maintains the record while the other person gets an always-current, read-only browser view without installing the app. Balance Sync is the two-way option: exactly two You Owe Me users can both update supported connected entries from their own phones.

### Can Live Link and Balance Sync be active for the same connected person?

Not at the same time. Use Live Link when one person maintains the record and the other person only needs browser visibility. Use Balance Sync when exactly two app users both need to update supported entries.

### How does someone connect with Balance Sync?

The sender opens a person, chooses Share and then Balance Sync, reviews what will be shared, and creates a private invitation by QR code or link. The invitation expires after seven days and should only be sent to the intended person. The recipient signs in, reviews the invitation and data disclosure, and accepts the balance into a new, separate person record.

### Does Balance Sync update instantly?

Do not treat it as instantaneous or real-time. Synchronization runs after local changes, when the app becomes active, when connectivity returns, and when someone manually refreshes or retries.

### What information synchronizes?

Balance Sync synchronizes the supported information needed to reproduce connected balance entries, including amount, debt direction, currency, date, note or reason, entry icon, archived status, and supported interest or linked balance-record information.

### What stays private on each phone?

The local name assigned to the person, profile images, entry images and attachments, reminders, recurrence rules, and other local-only settings are not copied to the other user.

### Does Balance Sync upload every old transaction?

No. It shares the history needed to reproduce the current balance accurately—normally entries since the most recent point when the two people were even. Older settled history usually stays only on the original device. If the app cannot reproduce the balance exactly, setup is rejected rather than creating an incorrect connection.

### What happens if both people edit the same entry?

Only that entry pauses. The user explicitly chooses which complete version to keep, preventing a silent overwrite. Other connected activity can continue normally.

### Does Balance Sync work with Group Paybacks?

Not currently. Balance Sync is for a supported balance between exactly two people. Group Payback activity does not synchronize.

### What happens when someone disconnects?

Future synchronization stops for both people and the same connection cannot be resumed. Entries already copied to each phone remain as ordinary local data, so disconnecting does not erase either person’s local history.

### How many Balance Sync connections are included?

The free plan supports one active or pending Balance Sync connection. Paid access removes the app-level connection limit. Existing connections continue working even when the user cannot create another one.

## Shared costs & schedules

For repeated household costs, one-time splits, recurring charges, and balances that keep changing. Try the free Running Balance Calculator to see how expenses and repayments update one current balance.

### Split Entry for shared expenses

Record one shared expense instead of rebuilding the same entry person by person. Choose the participants, enter the total once, include your own share when needed, and let YouOweMe turn the result into accurate entries for each real person.

Dinners, tickets, groceries, trips, rent, and client costs all end with clean individual balances, not manual math or duplicate records.

- One shared expense becoming separate balance entries

- Including yourself in the calculation without creating a debt to yourself

- Equal, visual, or exact custom shares for real-world fairness

### Group Paybacks for shared costs you paid for

Quick Split is useful when you only need to create one-time split entries. Group Paybacks are useful when the shared cost stays open. Create one Group Payback for the gift, tickets, dinner, deposit, or booking, then track who paid, who partially paid, and who still owes.

Each person’s share is still connected to their own running balance, so the shared record and the personal balance history stay aligned.

For a browser-only status check, try the Group Payback Calculator.

### Equal splits

Divide a shared bill evenly when everyone has the same share. If you were part of the expense too, include yourself in the math while saving entries only for the people who actually owe you.

- Meals, groceries, household supplies, and trip costs

- Shared expenses where your own share should be excluded

- Fast splits where fairness is straightforward

### Custom splits

When a shared expense is not evenly divided, assign each person the right share before saving. The app keeps the total reconciled and carries the correct amount into each person's balance.

- Different room sizes or rent shares

- Uneven groceries or travel contributions

- Couples or families with different agreements

### Visual and manual split control

For two or three participants, the draggable bubble view makes uneven shares feel quick and natural. For larger groups or receipt-based splits, manual entry gives exact amount control before anything is saved.

- Quick uneven splits when one person had more

- Exact receipt-based amounts for larger groups

- Shares that stay consistent if the total changes later

### Payment reminders

Set reminders for due dates, bills, balances, and follow-ups. A reminder can stay attached to a specific IOU, loan, a person's balance, or a standalone bill, so the nudge still knows what the money is for.

For an active repayment plan, the reminder follows the next unpaid installment. After a partial, full, or extra payment, it updates to the current amount and due date instead of repeating an outdated number.

When a reminder is tied to a person, YouOweMe helps you return to the right balance and choose the next step: record a payment when there is a fixed amount, mark it done, keep it, or follow up based on the current balance.

- Due dates tied to a specific entry, loan, repayment plan, or payback

- Standalone bill reminders for rent, utilities, subscriptions, invoices, or other payments

- Balance and follow-up reminders for people you need to review later

- Upcoming, overdue, completed, and recurring reminder states

### Recurring entries

Some money patterns are not one-offs. Rent, subscriptions, allowances, weekly coffees, monthly bills, and shared household costs tend to come back again and again.

Recurring Entries turns one entry into a schedule. Choose the rhythm from daily to yearly, keep it tied to the right weekday or calendar date, and optionally set when it should end. As each repeat comes due, the app creates a real entry so balances and history stay accurate.

- Rent, utilities, subscriptions, and allowances

- Every 2 weeks, every 3 months, or yearly repeats

- Repeated household costs that should update the real balance

### Rent, utilities, subscriptions, allowances, and repeated household costs

Use recurring entries and reminders together for the payments that keep returning. This is useful for roommates, couples, family reimbursements, and anyone who manages bills for someone else.

For a parent-specific example, see the elderly parent expense tracker or the parent-bill reimbursement workflow. For household costs, read how to track roommate bills and shared household costs.

- Roommate rent and utilities

- Parent subscriptions or online purchases

- Household costs that repeat but still need a clear balance

## Formal records

For larger balances, long-running records, clients, family reimbursements, or any situation where a more formal summary helps.

### PDF statements

Generate clean, shareable PDF statements from selected entries when you need a more formal summary. A focused loan PDF can show what was recorded, what was paid, what remains open, and the due date or payment details when needed. When a loan has a plan, you decide whether to include a concise repayment-plan summary with the next payment, regular rhythm, projected payoff, interest context, and overdue amount when relevant.

Statements reflect the real balance and history, not a manually rebuilt spreadsheet. Timeline can show when a PDF statement was shared, so the formal record stays connected to the rest of the history.

PDF statements are useful for summaries and records. They are not a replacement for accounting, tax, invoicing, or payment-processing software.

Starting manually? Download the Family Reimbursement Tracker Template for a simple Excel, CSV, or printable PDF log. If the record is mainly parent bills, subscriptions, groceries, pharmacy purchases, and sibling reimbursements, start with the Elderly Parent Expense Tracker.

- Client balances and small business records

- Family reimbursements that need a polished summary

- Long-term balances with percentage or fixed interest

### Logo, due dates, and payment details

Add your own logo or image, a due date, and payment details to a statement when the record needs to feel more professional or easier for a client to recognize. This is useful for freelancers, small service providers, tutors, coaches, and other simple client-payment situations where a branded summary is enough and a full invoicing system would be too much.

- Small business or freelancer summaries

- Client-facing repayment records

- Formal family reimbursement records

### Payment due dates

Add due dates when timing matters, then use reminders and statements to keep expectations clear. For client records, a due date can make the next step clearer on a PDF statement or shared summary without turning the record into a formal invoice.

- Repayment agreements

- Client or business balances

- Family reimbursements with a known payback date

### Interest tracking

Choose the interest mode that matches the agreement. Use percentage interest when the amount should grow over time: enter a rate, choose daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly frequency, and optionally set start and end dates. Use fixed or flat interest when you only need one exact amount added once, such as $10 or $25, with no rate or date calculation.

Once interest is saved on an entry, YouOweMe includes it in balances, entry totals, Loan Records, statements, shared links, and repayment context.

Repayment plans can instead use no new interest, one fixed total interest amount, or annual interest on the declining unpaid principal. Payments apply to unpaid interest first and then principal, so the projected payoff stays consistent with the plan terms.

- Percentage interest that grows over time

- Fixed interest or one-time extra amounts

- Clear repayment summaries with principal and interest context

### Long-running balances

YouOweMe is designed for money situations that do not finish in one transaction. The balance can move up or down as entries, repayments, splits, and adjustments happen.

- Family, roommate, couple, or client records over months

- Balances with partial repayments

- Situations where the history matters as much as the amount

### Client or small business records

Use YouOweMe for simple client balances and repayment records when you need clarity, not a full accounting or invoicing replacement. You can keep charges, deposits, partial payments, due dates, payment details, and client-facing PDF summaries connected to the same balance history. For the full workflow, see the Simple Client Payment Records solution.

- Freelancer repayment records

- Simple client payback histories

- Clear statements for balances both sides need to review

## Convenience, privacy, and reliability

Fast capture, offline access, privacy controls, and sync options help the app fit everyday use.

For a plain-English view of local records, optional cloud features, Live Links, AI tools, exports, reminders, and App Lock, read Privacy and Data in You Owe Me.

### Voice to Entry

Say something like "I lent Alex 30 euros for groceries yesterday." The app turns it into a structured entry with the right person, amount, category, and date.

- Fast capture when you are on the go

- Daily use without typing every detail

- Natural wording for real-world money moments

### App interface in seven languages

You can use the You Owe Me app interface in English, Arabic, French, German, Japanese, Portuguese, or Spanish.

Language availability applies to the app interface. This website is currently available in English only.

- English

- العربية

- Français

- Deutsch

- 日本語

- Português

- Español

### Works offline

Use YouOweMe even when you do not have a connection. This is useful when you need to record something immediately and do not want the moment to disappear.

- Travel, poor reception, or quick entry on the go

- Private records you want available on device

- Tracking without depending on a live web app

### No mandatory sign-up

Start tracking without being forced through an account wall. You can keep simple money records quickly when the need is immediate.

- Quick IOU tracking

- People who want less account friction

- Testing the app before using cloud features

### App Lock

Keep your repayment history private with App Lock. Unlock the app using Face ID, Touch ID, or your device passcode whenever you open it, so your balances and personal repayment records stay private even if someone else has your phone.

- Personal balances you want to keep private

- Family or client records on the same device

- Extra privacy for everyday finance data

### Sync across devices and multiple cloud profiles

Use cloud sync and multiple cloud profiles when you need records available across devices or want to keep different money contexts separate.

- Moving between iPhone and other Apple devices

- Separating personal, family, or client profiles

- Keeping important balances backed by cloud features

## Everything included

All the core tools for clear money records live in one place.

- Running balances

- Balance Replay

- Relationship Timeline

- Loan Records

- Repayment plans linked to Loan Records

- IOU tracking

- Split Entry for shared expenses

- Group Paybacks

- Partial repayments

- Payment reminders

- Recurring entries

- Smart Money Check-Ins

- Money Conversations

- Live Link

- Balance Sync between two users

- PDF statements

- Percentage and fixed interest tracking

- Voice to Entry

- CSV export

- Multi-currency support

- App interface localized in seven languages

- Sync across devices and multiple cloud profiles

- App Lock with Face ID, Touch ID, or device passcode

- Works offline

- No mandatory sign-up

## Use only the structure your situation needs

Start with a running balance. Add a separate loan or repayment plan when the amount, timing, or history needs more care—without moving the record into another system.

Want proof from real users first? See what users say about You Owe Me.

Money between people

# Find your money situation

Not every money situation starts with the right keyword. Maybe someone owes you, maybe you owe someone, maybe family helped with bills, or maybe roommates are splitting costs over time. Choose the situation that sounds closest, and we will point you to the most useful guide, tool, or tracker.

You Owe Me helps people keep money between real people clear without turning it into a bank, payment app, spreadsheet, or pressure-heavy conversation.

Start here

## Start with what sounds closest

These are the fastest paths for the situations people usually recognize before they know the exact tool or keyword.

### Someone owes me money

Start here when there is an open balance and you want a clear record or a calm follow-up.

- Generate a polite reminder

- Calculate a partial repayment

- Browse reminder examples

### I need to suggest a repayment plan

The balance is clear, but paying it all at once may not be realistic. Learn how to propose smaller repayments and confirm a plan both people understand.

- Calculate the payment steps

### I need to set up a clear record for one personal loan

Use this when repayment is understood, but you need to decide what to record, keep actual payments separate from planned installments, or begin after payments have already started.

Use when: you want a copyable recordkeeping method before choosing a tracker or app.

- Track actual repayments

- See the ongoing loan workflow

### Track one personal loan and its repayments

Keep the loan separate, record actual payments, and keep an optional repayment plan, remaining balance, next payment, reminder, and projected payoff current.

Use when: you lent or borrowed one larger amount and repayment will happen over time.

- Create the initial payment plan

- Suggest a repayment plan calmly

### I need to compare the repayment plan with actual payments

Use this when one personal loan already has a regular plan and real payments may be partial, extra, early, late, corrected, or followed by more borrowing.

Use when: A plan exists, but you need the truthful current balance, installment status, next payment, and projected payoff.

### I feel bad asking for my money back

Use this when someone owes you money, but you are not sure whether asking would be rude, petty, unfair, or relationship-damaging.

- Generate a polite reminder

- Track the open balance

- Ask without being rude

### I need to keep track of who owes what

Use this when the balance exists but the record is not clear yet: who owes whom, why, what was repaid, and what is still open.

- Calculate a partial repayment

- Compare tracking methods

- Open money-owed tracker

### I owe someone and need to repay clearly

Use this when you want to repay in steps, send an update, or show what has already been paid.

- Calculate what remains after partial repayments

- Send a repayment update

- Create a repayment receipt

### I need to ask a friend to borrow money

Use this when you need help from a friend and want to ask clearly, make “no” safe, and set repayment or check-in expectations before money moves.

- Create a support record

- Plan repayment

- Say no kindly if needed

- Track support over time

### Family helped with money

Use this when support between family members should stay clear without becoming awkward.

- Track family reimbursements

- Ask family for help clearly

### I pay for an elderly parent

Use this when you cover parent bills, subscriptions, groceries, pharmacy purchases, online orders, or household costs and need a record that family members can understand later.

- Read the parent-expense guide

- Use the family template

### Someone asked me for financial help

Use this when you may want to help someone close, but need the gift, repayment, boundary, or check-in expectation to stay clear.

- Create a support record

- Say no kindly if needed

### We never agreed whether the money was a gift or something to repay

Use this after money already changed hands and the repayment expectation was never clear—or the two people now remember it differently.

- Create a clarification message

- Read the helper-side guide

- Track agreed support over time

### A friend keeps borrowing money

Use this when the same friend keeps asking, old balances are still open, or small repeated amounts are starting to feel unclear.

- Say no politely

- Create a repayment plan

- Track the open balance

### Roommates are sharing costs

Use this for rent, utilities, groceries, household supplies, and repeated shared costs.

- Split roommate bills

- Read the roommate guide

### I paid first for a group cost

Use this when you covered a group gift, tickets, dinner, booking, deposit, or shared purchase and need to calculate shares, track paid / partly paid / still-open status, or send a calm group reminder without spamming everyone.

- Open Group Payback Tracker

- Read the group payback guide

- Remind the group without spamming everyone

- Split one expense

- Generate a reminder message

### The balance keeps changing

Use this when one payment or one note is no longer enough because both sides keep adding and repaying.

- Calculate a running balance

- Compare app tracking with spreadsheets

### I want to track shared money myself

Use this when you can keep the record, but the other person mainly needs an always-current balance, statement, receipt, or Live Link without installing another app.

- Calculate a running balance

- Compare shared expense apps and running balances

- See Live Link features

### I want to understand records, sharing, and cloud features

Use this when sensitive money records, optional sync, Live Links, AI tools, exports, reminders, or App Lock are part of the decision.

- Read the full Privacy Policy

- See how You Owe Me works

- Check whether the other person needs the app

### Clients are paying in steps

Use this when deposits, partial client payments, repeat service charges, or small work balances need a simple record without full accounting software.

- Use the Partial Repayment Calculator when one original client amount has deposits or partial payments.

- Calculate a running balance

- Create a repayment receipt

### I need a tool right now

Start with a calculator, template, generator, or receipt before deciding what to track long term.

- Split one expense

- Calculate partial repayments

- Create a repayment plan

- Generate a receipt

### I pay more than my partner

Use this when one partner keeps paying first or covering more of the shared costs, and you need to decide what should be ignored, split, reimbursed, carried forward, or treated as support.

- Calculate the current couple balance

- Open couples tracker

- Read the relationship spending guide

### We have not agreed how to split shared expenses

Compare 50/50, income-based, equal-leftover, and custom outcomes before choosing a contribution rule.

### I am not sure whether I need a note, calculator, spreadsheet, split app, or IOU tracker

Use this when you are choosing between notes, chat history, spreadsheets, payment history, calculators, shared expense apps, and You Owe Me.

- Compare spreadsheet vs app tracking

- Compare with Splitwise-style tracking

- Compare shared expense app vs running balance app

- See how You Owe Me works

Choose your starting point

## If you are still choosing, start here

The best route depends on whether you need a record, a calculation, wording, or a longer-term setup.

Reconcile or close

## When an existing money arrangement changed or needs to close

Start here when the original agreement no longer matches the current situation—because the history is disputed, a group cost changed, a family contribution rule is unclear, ongoing support needs to end, or shared expenses need a final closeout.

### Disagree about how much is still owed

Rebuild the expenses, repayments, offsets, and corrections row by row, then keep unresolved items outside the balance both people accept.

### Shared cost changed after someone canceled

Recalculate refunds, credits, resales, replacements, added charges, and revised shares before tracking who has paid.

### Siblings need a fair parent-expense contribution method

Compare equal, income-based, category-based, caregiver-credit, and hybrid methods before opening reimbursement balances.

### Ongoing financial support needs to end or taper

Separate future support from gifts, unclear past money, and any existing agreed repayable balance before changing the record.

### Shared expenses need a final closeout after a breakup

Set a cutoff date, identify only mutually understood shared expenses, count repayments, and confirm the final agreed balance.

Browse by situation

## Browse guides, tools, and solutions

Use the filters to narrow the page. All cards remain visible and crawlable without JavaScript.

Showing all situation cards.

### App to track money owed

Shows how You Owe Me keeps one clear record so follow-ups can be calmer and more specific.

Use when: someone needs an app for money owed between friends, family, partners, clients, or small groups.

Next step: Create a record in You Owe Me.

### Personal Loan Repayment Tracker

Shows how You Owe Me keeps one named loan, its actual payments, remaining balance, optional repayment plan, reminders, and history clear.

Use when: one larger amount will be repaid over time, or a loan already in progress needs a separate record.

### Personal Loan Payment Tracker

Record actual payments against an agreed plan and see the remaining balance, installment status, next payment, and projected payoff.

Use when: A repayment plan exists and you need to compare it with what actually happened.

Next step: Track actual repayments in the browser, then use the personal-loan solution when future payments and changes need to stay connected.

### Simple Client Payment Records

Helps freelancers, tutors, small service providers, and other people keep client charges, deposits, partial payments, and remaining balances clear.

Use when: client payments happen in steps or a simple work balance needs a private record.

Next step: Use the Partial Repayment Calculator when one original client amount has deposits or partial payments. Use the Running Balance Calculator when repeat charges keep being added.

Also useful: Create a repayment receipt after a payment, or compare spreadsheet tracking with app-based balance tracking.

### Family reimbursement tracker

Helps family members keep purchases, repayments, partial repayments, and recurring costs clear without relying on memory.

Use when: family costs repeat over time or multiple relatives need a calm record.

Next step: Use the family reimbursement tracker template.

Also useful: For recurring subscriptions and bills, read the recurring family bills guide.

### Elderly Parent Expense Tracker

Helps adult children, caregivers, and family members track parent bills, subscriptions, groceries, pharmacy purchases, sibling reimbursements, recurring charges, partial repayments, and monthly reviews.

Use when: one person pays for or manages elderly parent expenses and needs a calm record of what was paid, what repeats, what was reimbursed, and what still needs review.

Next step: Use the elderly parent expense tracker. If you want a manual starting point, use the family reimbursement tracker template.

Also useful: For parent bills and subscriptions that renew each month, read the recurring family bills guide.

### We need a fair way to share parent expenses

Compare contribution methods and create a sibling plan before tracking bills, reimbursements, or open balances.

Use when: Income, proximity, practical care, or recurring responsibilities differ and the family has not agreed on the rule.

### I pay recurring bills or subscriptions for family

Helps you track family phone plans, utilities, subscriptions, memberships, services, sibling shares, repayments, and monthly reviews without relying on memory.

Use when: one person pays recurring family charges and needs to see what repeats, what was repaid, and what is still open.

Next step: Start with the recurring family bill log, then use the family reimbursement tracker template if you want a manual record.

Also useful: Use the elderly parent expense tracker when the recurring bills are mainly for a parent.

### Roommate expense tracker

Helps roommates keep shared household costs and repayments clear across repeated bills.

Use when: roommates share repeated household costs and need a clear record.

Next step: Use the roommate bill split calculator.

### Temporary financial support tracker

Helps someone record temporary financial support, repayment expectations, updates, and remaining balance.

Use when: support has already been arranged and the people involved need a calm record of what happens next.

Next step: Use the temporary financial support record template.

### How to support someone financially without confusion

Helps the person giving support decide gift vs repayment, clarify expectations, set a check-in date, and keep the relationship calm.

Use when: someone close asks for financial help and the reader may want to help, but does not want vague expectations or memory to manage the situation later.

Next step: Create a simple support record if both people agree on the support.

### I need to stop ongoing financial support

Choose what ends, what may taper, and what happens to any existing agreed balance without turning past gifts into debt.

Use when: One person is already covering bills, rent, groceries, subscriptions, or other support and needs a clear transition.

Next step: Create the transition plan, then keep only any agreed continuing balance in the temporary-support workflow.

### Was the Money a Gift or a Loan? How to Clarify Calmly

Helps two people clarify whether money that already changed hands was a gift, fully repayable, partly repayable, flexible support, or still unresolved before either person records an outstanding balance.

Use when: Use this when money already changed hands but repayment was never clearly agreed, only part may be repayable, or the people involved now remember the expectation differently.

Next step: Clarify the expectation first, then record only the outcome both people understand.

### Shared expense tracker

Shows how one running balance can make repeated shared expenses easier to understand.

Use when: shared costs happen more than once and the balance should not be rebuilt from scattered notes.

Next step: Use the running balance calculator.

### Can One Person Track Shared Money Without Everyone Installing an App?

Explains when one person can keep the record and share a balance, statement, receipt, screenshot, or Live Link without forcing setup.

Use when: the other person mainly needs visibility, not editing access.

Next step: Calculate the current balance or start the record in You Owe Me.

### People paid at different times

Use this when different people paid first, someone paid back later, or a partial repayment changed the current balance.

Next step: Choose whether this needs a split calculator, running balance, group payback check, partial repayment calculator, or You Owe Me.

### Someone canceled after a shared cost was booked

Rebuild the final unrecovered cost after refunds, credits, resales, replacements, or added charges, then choose an allocation the group actually understands.

Use when: The group agreed on a cost before the amount or participant list changed.

Next step: Use the cancellation adjustment planner before tracking paybacks.

### Group Payback Tracker

Use this when you paid for a gift, tickets, dinner, deposit, booking, or shared purchase and need to see who paid, who partially paid, and who still owes.

Next step: Open the group payback tracker.

### Track who paid you back for a group expense

Use this when you paid first for a group cost and people are paying you back later.

Next step: Start with the guide, then use Group Paybacks if the payback list stays open.

Also useful: Use the Split Expense Calculator if you still need each person’s share.

### Couple Shared Expense Balance Calculator

Calculates a shared expense balance between two partners with 50/50, custom, income-based, category, paid-total, and transfer options.

Use when: partners need the current number before deciding whether to settle up, carry the balance forward, or start ongoing tracking.

Next step: Track couple expenses over time if this balance will keep changing.

### I Pay More Than My Partner for Shared Expenses

Helps you decide whether uneven partner spending should be ignored, split, reimbursed, carried forward, or treated as temporary support.

Use when: one partner keeps paying more often and the couple needs clarity without scorekeeping.

Next step: Start with the decision guide, then calculate the couple balance if the money should be shared or carried forward.

### We need to close shared expenses after a breakup

Set a cutoff date, separate agreed shared costs from gifts and personal spending, count repayments, and confirm the final everyday balance.

Use when: A relationship is ending but informal shared bills, subscriptions, reimbursements, or a running balance still need closure.

Next step: Use the final settlement checklist before calculating or tracking anything that remains open.

### Expense tracker for couples

Helps partners track shared spending, repayments, and running balances with less friction.

Use when: partners split bills, cover each other, or need a calm way to remember what happened.

Next step: Read the couples expense guide.

### The bill feels unfair because people ordered different amounts

Choose between an equal, itemized, hybrid, or separate-check split before calculating who owes what.

### Split expense calculator

Calculates who should pay whom after a shared expense is divided.

Use when: a person needs a free calculator before deciding whether to track the balance in the app.

Next step: Read the shared expense tracker solution.

### Repayment reminder text examples

Provides calm message examples for reminding someone about money without sounding confrontational.

Use when: someone owes money and the user wants to follow up without escalating the tone.

Next step: Generate a reminder with the polite payback reminder generator.

### Polite payback reminder generator

Generates a calm reminder that matches the relationship, tone, and repayment situation.

Use when: the user knows what needs to be said but wants help making the message clear and respectful.

Next step: Create a record in You Owe Me.

### Family reimbursement tracker template

Gives families a simple template for recording purchases, repayments, and remaining amounts.

Use when: a family needs a downloadable or printable record before moving to app tracking.

Next step: Read the family reimbursement tracker solution.

### Roommate bill split calculator

Helps roommates split a monthly set of bills, including optional fixed and usage portions, days present, guests, and agreed usage weights.

Use when: roommates need clear math for an ordinary month or an agreed adjustment when someone was away.

Next step: Read the roommate expense tracker solution.

### Repayment receipt generator

Creates a simple confirmation after money is paid back, including remaining balance when relevant.

Use when: a repayment has arrived and both people need a calm written summary.

Next step: Create a record in You Owe Me.

### Partial Repayment Calculator

Calculates what remains after one or more partial repayments against one original amount.

Use when: one known amount was repaid in parts and the user needs the remaining balance before sending an update, receipt, or payment plan.

Next step: Create a receipt if the payment just happened, create a payment plan if the remaining balance needs future steps, or track the balance in You Owe Me if repayments will continue.

Money between people, made clear

# Know who owes whom and what to say next

YouOweMe gives money between people one clear record: a running balance for everyday IOUs, separate records for personal loans, and repayment plans that stay current when payments do not go exactly as expected. Reminders, Timeline, Live Links, optional Balance Sync, and calm message tools keep the wider context together.

Use You Owe Me as an IOU tracker, personal loan tracker, or shared money record when notes and messages are no longer enough.

- See the real balance without checking old messages

- Plan a personal loan around a payment amount or payoff date that is realistic

- Know when to follow up with Smart Money Check-Ins

- Share an always-current Live Link without requiring the app—or use Balance Sync when both people want to update the balance

Clear numbers. Clear words. Less tension. Free download · works offline · no mandatory sign-up · app interface in 7 languages. Read Privacy and Data in You Owe Me.

Start with your situation

## What kind of money are you trying to keep clear?

Choose the closest match. You do not need the perfect category — You Owe Me is built around the balance, history, repayments, and next step between people.

### Someone owes me money

Track IOUs, partial repayments, due dates, reminders, and calmer follow-ups when a friend, family member, client, or roommate still owes you.

### Temporary support

Keep covered rent, bills, groceries, repayment steps, timing changes, and check-ins clear without making the situation feel heavier than it needs to.

### I pay for a parent or family member

Track parent bills, subscriptions, groceries, pharmacy purchases, online orders, sibling reimbursements, recurring charges, and repayments.

### We split costs as a couple

Keep groceries, travel, rent, subscriptions, uneven spending, and repayments clear without turning every purchase into a tense conversation.

### Roommates and household bills

Track rent, utilities, groceries, household supplies, recurring charges, repayments, and roommate settle-ups in one running balance.

### Shared expenses over time

For friends, trips, groups, and repeated shared spending where one quick split is not enough.

### Running balance calculator

Add expenses and repayments over time to see the current balance between two people.

### One quick split

Only need to divide one bill, meal, purchase, trip cost, or household expense?

## Choose what you need now

Start by matching the situation, calculating the current balance, or comparing methods. When the record will keep changing, open You Owe Me from the path that fits best.

Want proof first? Read real App Store reviews.

## What is You Owe Me?

You Owe Me is an iPhone app for tracking money between people. It helps with IOUs, shared bills, temporary support, informal loans, repayments, recurring costs, reminders, Live Links, PDF statements, and follow-up messages — so you can see who owes whom, what changed, and what to say next.

Use it when the amount does not stay simple: someone repays part, another cost is added, a due date changes, a recurring bill renews, or you need to share the balance without forcing the other person into the app.

## How YouOweMe keeps shared money clear

1

### Log what happened

Add money lent, money borrowed, bills paid, shared expenses, recurring costs, or repayments.

2

### See the balance and timeline

Every entry updates the balance. Timeline keeps the money story with that person organized beyond a simple transaction list.

3

### Follow up or share clearly

Check what already happened, then set a reminder for a due date, bill, balance, or follow-up, generate a calmer money message, send a Live Link, or create a PDF statement when the situation needs more clarity.

## Built for the moments when money gets messy

Running balances

### One running balance per person

Track money lent, borrowed, repaid, split, or covered in one history. As you scroll back, the balance updates with the entry you are viewing.

Loan Records

### Separate important loans

Give each loan its own name, remaining balance, updates, and status while the full balance with that person stays correct.

Repayment plans

### Choose a realistic path to repayment

Choose a regular amount, target date, or number of payments—or compare three practical options. As you record partial or extra payments, the plan updates what remains, the projected payoff, and the next reminder.

Smart Money Check-Ins

### Know when to follow up

Smart Money Check-Ins look at real balances, repayment progress, reminders, promised dates, shared statements, and silence to suggest when a balance needs attention.

Money Conversations

### Send the right message

Generate follow-up, ask-for-loan, and repayment-update messages from the real balance and history, with a tone that fits the relationship.

Need a one-time message first? Try the free Payback Reminder Generator or read how to remind someone they owe you money politely.

Live Link

### Share a live balance

Share one always-current statement link so the other person can see the latest balance and history in a browser without installing the app.

Balance Sync

### Two people. In sync.

Privately connect one balance between exactly two You Owe Me users, so supported connected entries changed on either phone stay aligned.

## Everything included

For simple IOUs or long-running balances, YouOweMe keeps the tools you need in one place, including percentage interest that grows over time and fixed interest added once.

## Why clear records matter

Money between people is common, but it can become stressful quickly. Bankrate's 2025 survey found that about 70% of U.S. adults have lent money or paid a group expense expecting to be reimbursed, and 55% of them experienced at least one negative consequence.

YouOweMe helps with the part you can control: the balance, the history, the reminder, and the next message.

Source: Bankrate

Family reimbursements are common too. The 2025 Caregiving in the U.S. report says 63 million Americans provide ongoing care, and AARP reports that half of caregivers experience a negative financial impact. Need a practical parent-bill workflow? See the elderly parent expense tracker or the parent expense tracking guide.

## FAQ

### What is You Owe Me?

You Owe Me is an iPhone app for tracking money between people. It helps with IOUs, shared bills, separate informal loans, repayment plans that follow real payments, recurring costs, reminders, Live Links, PDF statements, and follow-up messages.

### Is You Owe Me available on Android?

No. The You Owe Me app is available for iPhone only. There is no Android app or full browser version of the app. On Android, someone can still use the website’s free browser tools or open a read-only Live Link shared by a person using the iPhone app. Creating or editing an ongoing You Owe Me record requires the iPhone app, and Balance Sync is not available to an Android participant.

### Is YouOweMe only for loans?

No. It can track informal loans, IOUs, shared expenses, temporary support, family reimbursements, roommate bills, partner spending, client balances, recurring costs, and repayments over time.

### Can it help me ask someone to pay me back politely?

Yes. Money Conversations can generate a follow-up message from the real balance and history, with a tone that fits the relationship.

### Does the other person need the app?

Not always. Use Live Link when one person keeps the record and the other person only needs an always-current browser view without installing the app. Use Balance Sync when exactly two You Owe Me users both want supported connected entries to stay updated across their phones.

### Can I use it for family reimbursements?

Yes. You can track purchases, bills, subscriptions, recurring charges, and repayments for parents, siblings, children, or other family members. If the main job is paying for an elderly parent, start with the elderly parent expense tracker.

### Can I split bills and shared expenses?

Yes. You can split expenses equally or with custom amounts, then keep the result in a running balance instead of recalculating every time.

### What languages is the You Owe Me app available in?

The You Owe Me app interface is localized in seven languages: English, Arabic, French, German, Japanese, Portuguese, and Spanish. This applies to the app; the You Owe Me website is currently available in English only.

### Does it work offline?

Yes. YouOweMe can be used without mandatory sign-up and supports offline tracking.

## Keep money clear before it gets awkward

For everyday IOUs, keep one running balance and history. For a longer loan, keep the agreed plan, real payments, projected payoff, and next reminder tied to the same record.

Privacy & data clarity

# Privacy and Data in You Owe Me

A plain-English guide to what stays in the app, what can sync, what happens when you share a link, and how optional AI features work.

Money records are sensitive. You Owe Me is designed to help you keep a clear record of balances, repayments, shared expenses, reminders, notes, statements, and money conversations between real people. The core tracking experience can work without a mandatory You Owe Me account, and your working ledger is stored in the app's local database. Some features, such as iCloud sync, Cloud Accounts, Balance Sync, Live Links, temporary statement links, AI drafting, support, diagnostics, and exchange-rate lookup, use network services when you choose or enable them.

Free download. Core tracking works without a mandatory You Owe Me account.

Plain-English overview

## The short version

You Owe Me helps you keep records of money between people. The app is not a bank or payment processor. It does not move money, issue loans, collect debts, or report credit. It keeps a record of what happened, what was repaid, what is still open, and what you may want to say next.

### You can start without a cloud account

The core tracking experience does not require a You Owe Me cloud account. Some features, such as Cloud Accounts and Live Link management, use Sign in with Apple.

### Your ledger starts in the app

Your working ledger is stored in the app's local database and can support offline use for core tracking. Depending on your Apple account and device settings, it may also sync through iCloud.

### Sharing is a choice

PDFs, CSVs, text summaries, statement links, Live Links, and private two-person Balance Sync connections are created only when you choose to share or connect.

### AI drafts, you decide

AI-assisted features can help parse entries or draft messages, but the app shows results to you first. Messages are not sent automatically.

Records

## What the app helps you record

You Owe Me records the practical details needed to understand money between people later.

### People and balances

Names or labels, currencies, current balances, and the history connected to each person, client, family member, roommate, partner, or group situation.

### Entries and repayments

Amounts, dates, directions, reasons or notes, repayments, partial repayments, corrections, and recurring entries.

### Shared costs and Group Paybacks

Shared expenses, participants, split shares, who paid first, who paid back, who partly paid, and who still owes.

### Reminders and check-ins

Due dates, reminder purpose, reminder timing, and whether a reminder was completed.

### Statements and exports

PDF statements, CSV exports, text summaries, receipt-style confirmations, and sharing history when you create them.

### Optional AI/message context

When you use AI-assisted features, the app may use the text and balance context needed to parse an entry or draft a message.

Storage and services

## Where your records can be stored

The exact places involved depend on which features you use, which Apple account and device settings are active, and whether you enable cloud or sharing features.

Place

Used for

What to know

Core working ledger and app settings

Core tracking works around the app's local database and can be used without a mandatory You Owe Me cloud account.

Your local app data may sync through Apple iCloud/CloudKit depending on your Apple account and device settings.

Cloud Accounts / Firebase

If you use Cloud Accounts, selected account/profile and ledger data needed for that feature may be stored in Firebase services.

Balance Sync / Firebase

Cloud Firestore and Cloud Functions process and store canonical copies of supported shared entries so changes can be projected into both participants' app records.

Public web links

These are public link-based pages. Anyone with the link can view the shared statement while it is active.

When you use AI features, relevant text and context may be sent to You Owe Me's AI backend, which uses OpenAI.

Support and diagnostics

Support requests and reliability

Crash reporting and support messages help diagnose problems. The full Privacy Policy explains the current analytics configuration.

For the legal version, data-retention details, provider list, and privacy request options, read the full Privacy Policy.

Setup

## No mandatory You Owe Me account for core tracking

You can use the core tracking experience without creating a You Owe Me cloud account. That keeps setup simple: choose the person, add what happened, and let the app keep the balance and history clear.

Some features need account or cloud support. For example, Cloud Accounts and Live Link management may require Sign in with Apple. Balance Sync requires both participants to use full Apple-linked Firebase accounts so the app can authorize the private connection.

New to the app?

### Start with the Quick Start guide.

Understand the one-person, one-balance model before installing or setting up your first record.

Sharing

## What happens when you share a record

Sharing is always something you choose. The app can help you share different levels of detail depending on what the other person needs.

Share option

Best when

Privacy note

Text summary

You only need a simple balance update.

You choose where to paste or send it.

CSV export

You want a spreadsheet-style copy.

The file is created for export and then controlled by where you save or send it.

PDF statement

The record needs to look clearer than a chat message.

You choose when to generate and share it.

Temporary statement link

You want a short-term browser view.

Public to anyone with the link and intended to expire after 3 days.

Live Link

The balance may change and the other person needs the latest view.

Public to anyone with the link while active. It may update when related entries change.

Balance Sync

Both people use the app and want one supported balance to update in both records.

Private to two authenticated participants after acceptance. Before acceptance, anyone with the complete invitation link may be able to claim it.

### Live Links are convenient, but they are still links.

When you create a Live Link, You Owe Me publishes a read-only web statement at an unlisted link. The other person does not need to install the app or create an account, but anyone with the link can view the active statement. Only share it with people who should see that balance history.

If your main question is whether the other person needs the app, read how one person can keep the record and still share the balance clearly.

- A Live Link can show selected balance history, totals, dates, amounts, currencies, notes/reasons, and interest details where relevant.

- A Live Link may update as you add, edit, or delete related entries.

- You can stop sharing, which removes transaction rows from the public page, or delete the Live Link record.

- They are link-based statements, not signed-in account pages.

### Balance Sync is private, two-way sharing for two people.

Balance Sync is optional. When two authenticated participants connect one balance, Firebase Cloud Firestore and Cloud Functions process and store a private canonical copy of supported shared entries. Shared fields can include amounts, currencies, dates, reasons or notes, interest settings, archive state, and supported loan relationships.

- Both participants can create, edit, archive, or delete connected entries. Those changes are projected into each person's local app record when the app synchronizes.

- Keep the invitation private: anyone with the complete link may be able to claim it before it expires after seven days, is replaced, or is cancelled. The website does not display the inviter, amounts, notes, or other entry details.

- The recipient accepts the balance into a new, separate person record. Balance Sync does not merge into an existing record.

- Amount, debt direction, currency, date, note or reason, entry icon, archived state, and supported interest or linked balance-record information can synchronize.

- Local person names, profile images, entry images and attachments, reminders, recurrence rules, and other local-only settings are not transferred.

- The initial connection shares the history needed to reproduce the current balance, normally beginning after the latest even point. Older settled history normally stays local, and setup fails safely if the balance cannot be reproduced exactly.

- If both people edit the same entry, that entry pauses until a user chooses one complete version. Other connected activity can continue, and changes are not silently overwritten.

- Group Payback activity does not synchronize. Live Link and Balance Sync also cannot be active at the same time for the same connected person.

- The connected balance’s base currency stays fixed until disconnection.

- Disconnecting stops future sync. Both people keep their local borrower and entries, while the disconnected canonical ledger becomes inaccessible and is scheduled for deletion after a 30-day safety window.

- Deleting an account closes its Balance Sync connections and schedules controlled canonical data for deletion. It cannot remotely erase a copy that the other participant already downloaded into their own local app storage.

- To keep a deleted account or Cloud Account scope closed to stale devices, Firebase may retain an opaque deletion fence. It contains no ledger entries, amounts, notes, invitation tokens, raw user ID, or raw profile ID.

Balance Sync uses encrypted transport and Firebase platform storage protections. It is not end-to-end encrypted.

For the product overview, participation choices, and feature limitations, see Balance Sync on the Features page.

### Ready to keep a clearer record?

Start in the app, then share summaries, PDFs, statement links, Live Links, or a private Balance Sync connection only when they help.

AI-assisted tools

## AI features draft and parse, they do not send messages for you

You Owe Me includes optional AI-assisted tools such as Voice to Entry, follow-up message generation, repayment update generation, and ask-for-loan message generation. These features are meant to reduce friction when the record is clear but the wording or entry capture is hard.

When you use these features, the app may send the text and relevant balance context needed for that feature to You Owe Me's AI backend, which uses OpenAI. That context may include names or labels, amounts, currencies, dates, notes/reasons, balance state, relationship context, and previous generated text when needed for regeneration.

The result is shown to you first. You choose whether to save an entry, copy a message, share a draft, or do nothing. AI money messages are not automatically sent to the other person.

### Reminders and AI messages are different

Payment reminders notify you so you do not forget a due date, bill, repayment, or follow-up task. AI money messages generate draft text you can edit, copy, or share. A reminder does not automatically send a message to the other person.

For the broader product view, see the Features page. If the specific issue is repayment timing, read the repayment update guide.

Notifications

## Reminders notify you, not the other person

Payment reminders are for the app user. They can help you remember a payback date, bill, repayment, person-balance check-in, or follow-up task. A reminder may include useful details such as a name, amount, due timing, or reminder purpose.

You Owe Me does not automatically send reminder messages to the other person. If you decide to follow up, you stay in control of whether to write, edit, copy, or share a message.

### Due date reminder

Helps you remember a date or amount, not sent automatically.

### Person balance check-in

Helps you review an open balance, not sent automatically.

### Follow-up task

Helps you return to a conversation, not sent automatically.

Device protection

## App Lock helps protect records on your phone

You can turn on App Lock to require Face ID, Touch ID, or your device passcode before opening the app. This is useful when your phone contains personal, family, client, or repayment records you do not want visible to someone who picks up your device.

### App Lock

Face ID / Touch ID / passcode

Permissions

## Permissions are tied to optional features

### Contacts

Used when you choose to add people from Contacts.

### Camera / Photos

Used when you choose images for profiles, entries, or related records.

### Microphone / Speech Recognition

Used for Voice to Entry.

### Notifications

Used for reminders and app notifications.

### Face ID / device authentication

Used for App Lock.

### iCloud / Sign in with Apple

Used for Apple sync/account-related features.

You do not need every permission for every workflow. The app asks when a feature needs access.

Reliability

## Reliability and support data

The app uses crash reporting and diagnostics to help investigate reliability issues. If you contact support, your message and any details you choose to include may be used to respond and diagnose the issue.

If you need help with a privacy question or account-related request, use the support form.

### Current analytics wording

The app codebase includes Firebase Analytics, but the current Privacy Policy explains that Analytics collection is disabled in the bundled configuration for the app version that policy covers. Because this can depend on app version and configuration, the legal Privacy Policy is the source of truth for the current analytics status.

Boundaries

## What You Owe Me does not do

You Owe Me is a record and communication app. It helps you understand and explain money between people. It does not enforce, process, or legally formalize the money.

### a bank

### a lender

### a payment processor

### debt collection

### credit reporting

### accounting or tax software

### a legal contract system

### an invoicing platform

For formal loans, taxes, accounting, contracts, collections, or regulated financial services, use the appropriate professional tool or advisor.

Examples

## How this looks in real situations

### Friend owes you after several small costs

You keep the running balance in the app. If you need to follow up, you can copy a calm message or share a summary. The other person does not need an account just to understand the current balance.

### Family support or parent expenses

You can record what was paid, what was repaid, and what still remains open. If the situation continues, a clear record helps avoid relying on memory.

### Client-style payment record

You can keep a lightweight payment history and create a PDF statement or summary when the client needs context. You Owe Me still does not replace accounting, invoicing, tax, or payment-processing software.

### Live balance without another app

When another person needs visibility but does not want to install anything, a Live Link can show the active statement in a browser. It is useful, but it is public to anyone with the link.

Best next step

## Choose what you want to understand next

Privacy depends on what you use: local records, cloud profiles, sharing, AI drafting, exports, reminders, or App Lock. Start with the path that matches your concern.

FAQ

## Questions about privacy and data in You Owe Me
